title: Adaptive trace aggregation & helper scripts - notes
body:
Goal
- Capture representative end-to-end traces across hosts/pods without storing full traces for every request. We want an adaptive system that:
  * adjusts sampling frequency by endpoint and latency percentile
  * aggregates trace spans across multiple processes/pods into a compact summary
  * deduplicates repeated hot-paths (same callgraph signature)
  * emits artifacts for flamegraph and hotspot analysis (both CPU and scheduler stalls)

Motivation / problem statement
- Perf CI and on-cluster diagnostics both suffer from volume: at request rate X we get millions of spans/day. Storing raw traces is expensive and noisy.
- Current sampling is mostly uniform - misses rare high-latency tail events or over-samples chat generation startup.
- Need low-overhead on production (p99 SLOs) but still give engs actionable artifacts for triage.

High-level design notes
- Two-level sampling: local fast sampler + central aggregator.
  1) Local sampler (per process/pod): attaches short trace headers for sampled requests. Uses a lightweight reservoir (N per minute) keyed by route + model variant.
  2) Aggregator (sidecar or agent): receives sampled traces via unix domain socket / local grpc and performs merge/compact step. Stores a compacted protobuf summary rather than raw spans.
- Aggregation rules: merge spans with identical stack-signature and contiguous timestamps into a single summary: count, min/avg/max latency, sample of `n` raw spans for context.
- Adaptive feedback loop: aggregator reports back per-route sampling weights to local samplers via an LRU config channel (see scripts/agent-config-sync.sh). We adjust sample weight by p50/p95/p99 delta and by recent error rate.

Implementation scripts (working list)
- tools/local-sampler.py (python) -- runs inside the runtime binary container; exposes /tmp/sampler.sock; small lock-free ring buffer to hold N (default 32/min) trace references.
- tools/agg-collector.go -- agent that reads UDS and performs signature hashing + merge. Outputs .compact.gz files to /var/log/trace-compact/ for upload.
- tools/signature-extractor.sh -- uses perf-record stackwalk dumps + demangle to compute normalized call-signature.
- ci/trace-upload-and-flamejob.yaml -- perf CI job that pulls compacted artifacts from S3 and runs flamegraph generation + diff against baseline.
- infra/agent-config-sync.sh -- small updater to push new sampling weights to nodes (k8s configmap or systemd socket).

Runbook: quick triage (operator)
1) If high p99 observed on console route `/v1/generate`: check operator panel -> sampling-rate for that route (console/route panel). If zero, bump to 1% for 10 minutes to get traces.
2) On an affected host, check local sampler socket: sudo socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/sampler.sock; send "status" command -> returns counts/last-sample-id.
3) Pull compact artifacts: ssh node -> sudo cat /var/log/trace-compact/latest.compact.gz | zstd -d | jq '.' (compact format includes fields: signature, count, p50, p95, p99, attachments[0..2])
4) If signature count >> baseline and p99 delta > 2x, run tools/signature-extractor.sh against that host to get full perf.data snapshot for deeper analysis.

Perf CI integration notes
- Job flow: 
  * nightlies take baseline compact artifacts from `s3://redwood-perf/baselines/<branch>` and compare to current run.
  * aggregator outputs are turned into per-endpoint flame SVGs using flamegraph.pl and node-annotate (we maintain a custom annotate script to label model/kvcache boundaries).
  * For diffs, we compute KS test on signature latency distributions and fail job only if there is a statistically significant regression on top-k signatures.
- Resource sizing: agg-collector runs as DaemonSet with 100Mi memory and 0.5 CPU by default. If you see OOMs, bump to 250Mi. The compacting step uses ~50MB of transient memory per 1000 unique signatures.

Aggregation compact format (human readable description)
- text rows (one per signature) with tab fields: signature_hash \t count \t min_ms \t p50_ms \t p95_ms \t p99_ms \t sample_span_ids(comma) \t host_tag
- attachments: stored separately in attachments/ as compressed JSON blobs (kept for only top-3 per signature).

Diagnostics & debugging tips
- Warm startup: if many short-lived signatures appear during binary startup, we filter signatures with lifespan < 5s and count < 3 to avoid noise.
- KV cache hotpath: signatures that include 'kvcache::get' followed by 'attention::forward' should be grouped and annotated as KV-miss vs KV-hit by scanning span attributes. Add heuristics in signature-extractor to mark misses.
- When you see UID-level variance across hosts, check if aggregator time drift is > 200ms (we had a bug where host clock skew produced duplicate signatures). Ensure ntp/chronyd running.

Script examples (cheat sheet)
- Trigger a local sample: 
  echo \"sample route=/v1/generate ctx=live\" | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/sampler.sock
- Dump last compact file: 
  zstd -d /var/log/trace-compact/latest.compact.gz | sed -n '1,200p'
- Convert compact -> flame input: 
  scripts/compact-to-flame.sh latest.compact.gz > flame.in
  flamegraph.pl --color=io flame.in > flame.svg

Open questions / TODOs (short list)
- Decide retention policy for attachments: 7 days? 14? impacts cost significantly.
- How to attribute cross-host RPC spans (we currently tag by trace-id but aggregation loses original host ordering). Maybe keep a small vector clock in signature.
- Evaluate eBPF offload to gather kernel-level scheduler stalls and merge into signature (Rina to prototype).

Recent changes / notes
- 2024-10-15: switched signature hash from fnv64 to xxh3 for better distribution; reduced collision noise. (PR #1345)
- 2024-10-20: aggregated attachments moved to compressed blob store to reduce file count.

Related tickets and links
- INF-827: "adaptive trace aggregation PoC" (links in header)
- PR: runtime/pull/1345 - agg-collector initial impl
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime (thread: "trace-agg perf noise")

Checklist before flipping to higher sampling in prod
- [ ] infra provisioning for S3 upload + lifecycle rule in staging
- [ ] CI job to validate compact format version bump (schema v2)
- [ ] Alert: compact upload failures > 5/min escalate to oncall
- [ ] Run controlled canary on dedicated region for 48h

Notes to self (Avery)
- Keep samples small: only store full request payload for 1/50th of attachments to limit PII exposure.
- Add a script to rehydrate compact->trace for local sandbox so engineers can click-through from console to full trace in a dev environment.
- Follow up with SRE about chrony config on k8s nodes (drift seen in staging last week).

Unresolved artifacts (placeholders)
- tools/compact-to-flame.sh (stubbed, needs robust demangling)
- perf-ci job for windows-hosted runners (not yet implemented)

-- end of notes --

(Free-form, intentionally incomplete — this doc is a scratchpad for the PoC and orchestration scripts. If you are picking this up, ping me on Slack and I'll walk through the collector logs.)
